center.source: 01-RESEARCH.md 'Code Examples' worked example for the Orly-Ville/runway-3 area (48.7233N, 2.3794E), cross-checked against the English Wikipedia 'Orly Airport' infobox coordinate field (48°43'24"N 02°22'46"E → 48.7233, 2.3794 decimal). Used as the query center/radius origin, not the runway itself - the corridor below is the actual runway-3 filter. Checked 2026-08-04.

bbox.source: Computed (not looked up) from the confirmed runway-3 threshold coordinates in 'runway' below: extended roughly 2.5km beyond each threshold along the runway's own bearing (~074/254 TRUE) to include the on-approach and rollout segments, plus a lateral margin. Values unchanged since 2026-08-04 so that adsb-test/RESULTS.md's recorded Phase 1 sampling geometry stays true; this is now a COARSE PRE-FILTER ONLY - 'corridor' below is what actually decides whether an aircraft is on runway 3. Checked 2026-08-04.
bbox.correction_2026_08_27: This block previously claimed the box was 'tight enough to exclude the crossing 02/20 runway' and merely 'not perfectly exclusive' of 06/24. Both claims were measured against real published OurAirports LFPO geometry during the runway3-false-positive debug session and are WRONG. This axis-aligned box is 8078m x 2449m = 19.8 km2 around a 3.3 km runway, and it contains 1935m of runway 02/20's 2403m (80.5%, including runway 02's threshold at 48.717499/2.376700) and 2621m of runway 06/24's 3647m (71.9%). Its corners reach 2229m cross-track from runway 3's centreline. Two real aircraft using OTHER Orly runways were caught being selected as 'runway 3' by a 22-poll live capture on 2026-08-27 (a runway-20 departure at 750m off-centreline and a 02/20-aligned arrival at 611m). Do not treat 'in bbox' as 'on runway 3'.

corridor.source: Runway-aligned corridor around the 07/25 centreline defined by the two thresholds in 'runway' below (bearing 74.41 TRUE, length 3315m as computed from those coordinates). An aircraft counts as 'on runway 3' when its along-track position is within [-extension_m, length + extension_m] of threshold 07, its perpendicular (cross-track) offset from the centreline is <= half_width_m, and - when the record carries a numeric `track` - that true track is within axis_tolerance_deg of 074.41 or 254.41.
corridor.threshold_derivation: Both numbers are read off MEASURED separation between real runway-3 traffic and real wrong-runway traffic, not guessed. half_width_m=500: every real runway-3 aircraft available measures <= 31m cross-track (committed fixtures 39d300 +3.1m, 39dd01 +14.3m, 3985a7 +31.0m; live 2026-08-27 captures 347288 +3.0m and 39cea8 +2..+7m), while every real wrong-runway aircraft observed measures >= 611m (3964e8 -611.3m, 39de4a -750.4m) and runway 06/24's paved surface never comes closer than 887m. 500 therefore sits inside an empty 580m band - 16x above the largest real runway-3 offset and 1.8x below the nearest wrong-runway pavement. axis_tolerance_deg=30: real runway-3 traffic measured 0.0-0.7 deg off axis; real 02/20-aligned traffic measured 56.0-56.7 deg (02/20's axis is 56 deg from runway 3's by construction), so 30 sits inside an empty 55 deg band.
corridor.why_both_gates: Neither gate alone is sufficient, and this is a property of Orly's real layout rather than a belt-and-braces choice. Runway 06/24 is only 12 deg off runway 3's heading (062/242 vs 074/254), so a track gate CANNOT separate it - but its surface stays >= 887m from runway 3's centreline, so the corridor gate can. Runway 02/20 physically CROSSES runway 3's centreline (minimum cross-track 0m, at 1601m along, i.e. mid-runway), so the corridor gate CANNOT separate it - but it is 56 deg off runway 3's heading, so the track gate can. Each gate is blind to exactly the runway the other one catches.
corridor.known_residuals: (1) A record carrying no numeric `track` is not disqualified by the alignment gate - it still has to pass the corridor. Measured 21/21 (100%) of live adsb.fi records on 2026-08-27 carried a numeric track, and the pre-existing committed fixtures carry none at all, so this is deliberately permissive rather than a hard reject. (2) An aircraft taxiing on a runway-parallel taxiway (~150-200m offset, runway-aligned track) still passes both gates; tightening half_width_m below ~150m would start rejecting genuine approach traffic, so this residual is documented rather than closed. Checked 2026-08-27.

runway.source: OurAirports open aviation data, runways.csv (https://davidmegginson.github.io/ourairports-data/runways.csv), row with airport_ident=LFPO, le_ident=07 / he_ident=25, length_ft=10892 (=3320.0m exactly), le_latitude/le_longitude and he_latitude/he_longitude as recorded above. Cross-checked against the English Wikipedia 'Orly Airport' article infobox (r3_number=07/25, r3_length_m=3,320), which independently corroborates the exact 3320m length for this runway. Note: PROJECT.md's earlier text informally called this runway '08/26' with the same ~3,320m length; the confirmed ICAO heading-pair designator from both sources above is 07/25. Because the length matches exactly across two independent sources and no other Orly runway has this length, 07/25 is treated as the confirmed identity for 'runway 3' rather than the earlier informal '08/26' label - this correction should be carried into any later document update per D-03. Checked 2026-08-04.
runway.correction_2026_08_27: This block previously described the 074/254 heading pair as MAGNETIC. It is not: OurAirports supplies those figures in the le_heading_degT/he_heading_degT columns, i.e. degrees TRUE (074/254 for 07/25, 062/242 for 06/24, 018/198 for 02/20), and the bearing computed directly from the two threshold coordinates above is 74.41 TRUE. The distinction matters because the alignment gate compares against ADS-B's `track` field, which is true track over ground - the same records' `mag_heading` runs ~4 deg lower (249-254 vs a track of 254.2-254.9 for the real runway-25 arrival captured on 2026-08-27), and adsb.fi's `dir` field is not a heading at all but the bearing from the query centre to the aircraft. Verified 2026-08-27.

neighbouring_runways.note: Recorded here because runway 3 cannot be identified without knowing what it must be distinguished FROM. Same OurAirports LFPO rows, same download (2026-08-27). Used by server/test_plane_detection.py as a geometry regression: these coordinates must never be accepted as runway 3.

corridor.threshold_status: UNVALIDATED (Assumption A1, 06-RESEARCH.md): these three numbers are copied verbatim from runway 3's measured corridor derivation, not independently re-derived from real captured traffic on runway 06/24, and have never been checked against a single real capture on this runway. Runway 3's own numbers came from comparing real runway-3 traffic (measured at or below 31 m cross-track) against real wrong-runway traffic (measured at or above 611 m); no equivalent dataset exists for this runway. Plan 06-12 is the live-capture pass that either confirms these values or replaces them.

06-24.geometry_caveat: Runway 06/24 sits only 12 degrees off runway 3's heading (062/242 vs 074/254 TRUE), so a track-alignment gate alone cannot separate 06/24 traffic from runway-3 traffic - the same asymmetry recorded in the legacy corridor.why_both_gates for the reverse case (rejecting 06/24 traffic while tracking runway 3). When 06/24 is the tracked runway, it is the corridor gate that must do the separating instead (runway 3's own pavement never comes closer than 887m to 06/24's centreline); that reversed asymmetry is precisely why plan 06-12's live capture on this runway matters.

corridor.threshold_status: UNVALIDATED (Assumption A1, 06-RESEARCH.md): these three numbers are copied verbatim from runway 3's measured corridor derivation, not independently re-derived from real captured traffic on runway 02/20, and have never been checked against a single real capture on this runway. Runway 3's own numbers came from comparing real runway-3 traffic (measured at or below 31 m cross-track) against real wrong-runway traffic (measured at or above 611 m); no equivalent dataset exists for this runway. Plan 06-12 is the live-capture pass that either confirms these values or replaces them.

02-20.geometry_caveat: Runway 02/20 physically crosses runway 3's centreline (minimum cross-track ~0m, roughly mid-runway), so a corridor gate alone cannot separate 02/20 traffic from runway-3 traffic there - the same asymmetry recorded in the legacy corridor.why_both_gates for the reverse case (rejecting 02/20 traffic while tracking runway 3). When 02/20 is the tracked runway, it is the track-alignment gate that must do the separating instead (02/20 is 56 degrees off runway 3's heading); that reversed asymmetry is precisely why plan 06-12's live capture on this runway matters.

runways_source: Added by phase 6 plan 06-02 for CFG-12. The 'runways' block above supersedes the flat runway/corridor pair as the live source consulted by server/plane/detect.py's runway-parameterised functions (runway_axis()/corridor_params()/runway_block()); that flat runway/corridor pair is preserved unchanged as the legacy fallback path and as the historical record of the runway3-false-positive fix. Runway 3's entry in 'runways' (id "3") deliberately duplicates the legacy runway/corridor coordinates rather than referencing them, so a drift check (server/test_plane_detection.py) can assert byte-for-byte equality between the two and catch any future accidental divergence. Kept as a sibling of 'runways' rather than a key inside it so that 'runways' itself stays exactly the three runway-id keys server/plane/detect.py's runway_ids() enumerates.
